card: This pull request introduces the setprunelock and listprunelocks RPCs and a -prunelock=<id> startup option for manual prune lock management. It resolves the problem on pruned nodes where unloading a wallet or taking an external wallet or indexer offline allows blocks needed for rescans to be pruned away. The implementation reuses the existing internal prune lock subsystem with a user-specific prefix, keeping locks in memory for the duration of the node process.
changed_since_previous: The startup option was renamed from `-prunelockheight` to `-prunelock=<id>` (which initializes the lock at height 0 for later adjustment via RPC), and a functional test covering unloaded wallet rescan preservation was added.
evidence: PR description: 'On pruned nodes, if a wallet is not loaded while the node is running, blocks necessary for rescanning when the wallet is loaded may be pruned. This PR allows users and external wallet software to manually manage prune locks via RPC, so they can protect blocks needed for future rescans and also clean up locks that are no longer relevant...'
problem: When a wallet is unloaded on a pruned node while the node continues running, blocks required for rescanning when the wallet is reloaded can be pruned away. External wallets and indexers also lack an interface to keep blocks on disk temporarily without disabling pruning entirely or risking race conditions with pruning during node startup.

risk.why: Bugs in block storage prune lock accounting could unintentionally allow blocks needed for rescans to be deleted or prevent block deletion, leading to disk exhaustion.

summary: Adds `setprunelock` and `listprunelocks` RPCs alongside a `-prunelock=<id>` startup option, allowing users and external software to manually manage block prune locks. These locks prevent `BlockManager` from deleting block files at or above a specified height, are namespaced with a `user:` prefix to avoid collisions with internal locks, and exist only in memory across node runs.
